title: The Sunday Read: ‘Why Are These Italians Massacring Each Other With Oranges?’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜店打碟时，你每晚也会带上300件你最珍爱的宝贝去工作，并把DJ台……

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个美丽的、拥有50年历史的文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is John Mualem, and I'm a contributing writer to The New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫约翰·穆阿利姆，《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: For today's Sunday read,
sentences.zh: 在今天的周日阅读中，

sentences.en: I'm going to share a story I wrote for the magazine's Voyages issue about my trip to a small town in northern Italy for what has to be one of the world's most peculiar festivals,
sentences.zh: 我将分享我为该杂志“远航”特辑撰写的一个故事，讲述我去意大利北部一个小镇的旅行，那里有可以说是世界上最奇特的节日之一，

sentences.en: basically a three-day historical food fight.
sentences.zh: 基本上是一场为期三天的历史性食物大战。

sentences.en: So here's my story from the March 26, 2023
sentences.zh: 以下是我2023年3月26日的故事

sentences.en: New York Times Magazine,
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报杂志》，

sentences.en: The Voyages issue.
sentences.zh: “远航”特辑。

sentences.en: It looked as if a war was coming.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像要爆发一场战争。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: One Sunday last month, in a northern Italian town called Ivrea, the facades of historic buildings were covered with plastic sheeting and nets.
sentences.zh: 上个月的一个星期天，在意大利北部一个叫伊夫雷亚的小镇，历史建筑的正面都盖上了塑料布和网。

sentences.en: Storefront windows had been fortified with plywood and tarps.
sentences.zh: 店面窗户用胶合板和防水布加固了。

sentences.en: And in several different piazzas, hundreds of wooden crates had appeared, walls of them stacked eight feet high and even farther across.
sentences.zh: 在几个不同的广场上，出现了数百个木箱，它们筑成八英尺高、甚至更宽的墙。

sentences.en: The crates looked like barricades, but were actually arms depots.
sentences.zh: 这些木箱看起来像路障，但实际上是军火库。

sentences.en: Inside them were oranges.
sentences.zh: 里面装的是橙子。

sentences.en: Oranges.
sentences.zh: 橙子。

sentences.en: The fruit.
sentences.zh: 水果。

sentences.en: Over the next three days,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三天里，

sentences.en: 8,000 people in Ivrea would throw 900 tons of oranges at one another, one orange at a time, while tens of thousands of other people watched.
sentences.zh: 伊夫雷亚的8000人将向彼此投掷900吨橙子，一次扔一个，同时有几万人围观。

sentences.en: They would throw the oranges very hard, very viciously, often while screaming profanities at their targets or yowling like Braveheart.
sentences.zh: 他们会非常用力、非常恶劣地扔橙子，经常向目标大声咒骂，或者像《勇敢的心》那样嚎叫。

sentences.en: And they would throw the oranges for hours until their eyebrows were matted with pulp and their shirts soaked through.
sentences.zh: 他们会连续几个小时地扔橙子，直到他们的眉毛上沾满果肉，衬衫被完全浸透。

sentences.en: But they would also keep smiling as they threw the oranges, embracing and joking and cheering one another on, exhibiting with their total beings
sentences.zh: 但他们在扔橙子时也会保持微笑，拥抱、开玩笑并互相鼓励，用他们的全部身心表现出

sentences.en: a deranged-seeming but euphoric sense of abandon and belonging, a freedom that was easy to envy but difficult to understand.
sentences.zh: 一种近乎疯狂但又 euphoric（欣快）的纵情与归属感，一种易于羡慕却难以理解的自由。

sentences.en: The Battle of the Oranges is an annual tradition in Ivrea and part of a larger celebration described by its organizers as the most ancient historical carnival in Italy.
sentences.zh: 橙子大战是伊夫雷亚的一项年度传统，也是组织者所描述的意大利最古老的历史狂欢节的一部分。

sentences.en: Three years ago, things kicked off as they always do, with a few initial hours of hurling and splattering.
sentences.zh: 三年前，活动像往常一样拉开帷幕，进行了最初几个小时的投掷与飞溅。

sentences.en: But then the rest of the battle was abruptly called off.
sentences.zh: 但随后，其余的战斗被突然取消。

sentences.en: COVID had surfaced in the region and after an emergency meeting of government officials that afternoon, the decision was made to shut the festival down.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情在该地区出现，那天下午政府官员召开紧急会议后，做出了关闭节日的决定。

sentences.en: Several people in Ivrea told me that as two more pandemic years passed in which no oranges could be thrown, they grew concerned that something bad would happen in the community.
sentences.zh: 伊夫雷亚的好几个人告诉我，随着又是两年无法投掷橙子的疫情岁月过去，他们开始担心社区会发生不好的事情。

sentences.en: That without this catharsis, a certain pent-up sinister energy would explode.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这种宣泄，某种压抑的险恶能量将会爆发。

sentences.en: But it didn't.
sentences.zh: 但它没有。

sentences.en: They'd made it.
sentences.zh: 他们挺过来了。

sentences.en: And now, the scent of stockpiled citrus was mixing with the musk of centuries-old masonry.
sentences.zh: 现在，囤积的柑橘的气味正与拥有数百年历史的砖石的麝香味混合在一起。

sentences.en: The arancheri, or orange throwers, were standing by.
sentences.zh: arancheri（掷橙者）们正待命。

sentences.en: Ivrea's arancheri are organized into nine teams, each with a different flag, logo, captain, and uniform.
sentences.zh: 伊夫雷亚的掷橙者分为九个队伍，每支队伍都有不同的旗帜、标志、队长和制服。

sentences.en: They have names like the devils, the mercenaries, the Black Panthers, death.
sentences.zh: 他们有着诸如恶魔、雇佣兵、黑豹、死神之类的名字。

sentences.en: As 2pm approached, the arancheri crammed shoulder-to-shoulder in their assigned piazzas, each waiting to do battle with 47 brigades of other orange throwers who had come marauding
sentences.zh: 随着下午2点的临近，掷橙者们肩并肩地挤在各自分配的广场上，等待与47个其他掷橙者旅进行战斗，这些旅乘着马车

sentences.en: through the city in horse-drawn carts.
sentences.zh: 在城中四处劫掠。

sentences.en: Many had been partying until 2 or 3am the night before, and many were drinking that morning, too.
sentences.zh: 许多人前一晚狂欢到凌晨2点或3点，许多人那天早上也在喝酒。

sentences.en: The city was awash in disposable cups of mulled wine and Bombardino, a boozy, eggnoggy concoction, served warm.
sentences.zh: 城里到处都是装满热红酒和Bombardino（一种温暖的、带酒精的蛋酒混合饮料）的一次性纸杯。

sentences.en: They were predominantly men, especially young men, though there were many women, too.
sentences.zh: 他们主要是男性，尤其是年轻男性，不过也有很多女性。

sentences.en: There were also older people who had been participating in the Battle of the Oranges since they were the age of those young people.
sentences.zh: 还有一些老年人，他们从和这些年轻人一样大的时候就开始参加橙子大战了。

sentences.en: Some had taken those young people to their first battles in strollers
sentences.zh: 有些人曾在

sentences.en: 20-odd years ago.
sentences.zh: 20年前把这些年轻人用婴儿车推去参加他们的第一场战斗。

sentences.en: One woman showed me a photo with pride.
sentences.zh: 一位女士自豪地向我展示了一张照片。

sentences.en: In a neighborhood known as the Borghetto, a team called the Tucchini polished off compostable bowls of pasta in their small piazza, waiting in their green jerseys
sentences.zh: 在一个被称为博尔盖托的街区，一个叫图奇尼的团队在他们的小广场上吃完了可堆肥碗里的意大利面，他们穿着绿色球衣

sentences.en: with poofy sleeves and lace-up fronts.
sentences.zh: 带有蓬松的袖子和系带的前襟。

sentences.en: Over their heads hung a banner.
sentences.zh: 他们的头顶挂着一条横幅。

sentences.en: In the heart of the battle, we are never alone.
sentences.zh: 在战斗的核心，我们永不孤单。

sentences.en: Here's what happened next.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情是这样的。

sentences.en: The atmosphere in the Borghetto contracted like a fiSt.
sentences.zh: 博尔盖托的气氛像拳头一样收紧了。

sentences.en: Around the corner, the first carriage approached, barreling across the cobblestone bridge that connects the neighborhood to the rest of the city.
sentences.zh: 拐角处，第一辆马车驶近，在连接该街区与城市其他部分的鹅卵石桥上疾驰而过。

sentences.en: You could hear the low rumble of its wheels on stone, the bells on the horse's bridles, jingling madly.
sentences.zh: 你能听到它的车轮在石头上的低沉隆隆声，马勒上的铃铛疯狂地叮当作响。

sentences.en: As soon as the carriage appeared, the fusillade and the screaming started simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 马车一出现，齐射和尖叫声便同时响起。

sentences.en: Much of the crowd rushed to its flanks.
sentences.zh: 大批人群冲向它的两侧。

sentences.en: Inside the carriage, about half a dozen people dressed as medieval soldiers, their heads and faces disguised by creepy leather helmets adorned with braids, were already
sentences.zh: 马车里大约有半打人打扮成中世纪士兵，他们的头部和面部被带有辫子的可怕皮革头盔掩盖，已经

sentences.en: side-arming oranges mercilessly with both hands, their thick forearms pumping like pistons, their emptied fists reloading from the troughs at their waists while the opposite fists
sentences.zh: 用双手毫不留情地用侧手投掷橙子，他们粗壮的前臂像活塞一样上下泵动，空空如也的拳头从腰间的槽里重新装填，而另一边的拳头则

sentences.en: discharged.
sentences.zh: 进行发射。

sentences.en: They chucked oranges in a kind of balletic flow state, the brutal apparatuses of their torsos swiveling efficiently but hard.
sentences.zh: 他们以一种芭蕾般的流畅状态猛掷橙子，他们躯干残酷的结构高效而有力地转动着。

sentences.en: They threw straight down, punishing the people only two feet below, who, in turn, threw relentlessly upward at them.
sentences.zh: 他们直向下砸，惩罚着仅仅两英尺下方的人，而后者反过来又对他们进行毫不留情的向上抛掷。

sentences.en: Oranges sprayed through the air omnidirectionally like sawdust, like sparks.
sentences.zh: 橙子像锯末、像火花一样在空气中全方位喷洒。

sentences.en: The carriage came to a full stop at the center of the square.
sentences.zh: 马车在广场中央完全停了下来。

sentences.en: The battle reached a higher intensity.
sentences.zh: 战斗达到了更高的强度。

sentences.en: Oranges splattered off the soldiers' heads and rolled off their backs in sheets.
sentences.zh: 橙子砸在士兵的头上碎裂，成片地从他们的背上滚落。

sentences.en: The scene is so chaotic that once, a decade ago, a thrower in one of the carriages had a heart attack but no one noticed his body slumped there until they were
sentences.zh: 这一幕是如此混乱，以至于十年前，车上的一名掷橙者曾突发心脏病，但直到他们

sentences.en: getting out of the carriage.
sentences.zh: 下车时，都没有人注意到他的身体瘫倒在那里。

sentences.en: When the carriage started moving again, exiting the piazza, the diehards gave chase.
sentences.zh: 当马车重新开始移动、驶出广场时，死忠粉们追了上去。

sentences.en: They yelled at it through a froth of spittle and pith.
sentences.zh: 他们在白沫和果皮中向它大喊大叫。

sentences.en: In the calm that followed, people scampered around to claim oranges off the ground that looked intact enough to be relaunched.
sentences.zh: 在随后的平静中，人们四处奔跑，在地上捡那些看起来还算完好、可以重新发射的橙子。

sentences.en: Then, the next carriage arrived and everything that just happened happened again.
sentences.zh: 然后，下一辆马车到达，刚才发生的一切又重演了一遍。

sentences.en: I had the opportunity to participate that first afternoon though I'd been given zero instructions or tips.
sentences.zh: 我有幸在第一个下午参与其中，尽管我没有得到任何指示或提示。

sentences.en: Ordinarily, our and charity must register with the team weeks in advance and pay the roughly
sentences.zh: 通常，我们的掷橙者必须提前数周在团队注册并支付大约

sentences.en: 120 euro fee.
sentences.zh: 120欧元的费用。

sentences.en: But someone from the historic
sentences.zh: 但历史悠久的

sentences.en: Carnival of Ivrea
sentences.zh: 伊夫雷亚狂欢节

sentences.en: Foundation, which organizes the event, had simply gifted me an emasculatingly oversized zucchini jersey and wished me luck.
sentences.zh: 基金会（组织该活动）的一位人士只是赠予了我一件大得令人自惭形秽的超大西葫芦球衣，并祝我好运。

sentences.en: I took up a position on the periphery, tossing the occasional orange from long range, feeling giddy when my first one thwacked into a soldier's helmet and liquefied spectacularly.
sentences.zh: 我在边缘占据了一个位置，从远处偶尔扔一个橙子，当我的第一个橙子砸中士兵的头盔并壮观地化为液体时，我感到一阵头晕目眩。

sentences.en: What I hadn't understood though is that many people were winging oranges at the carriages from similar distances and from all directions.
sentences.zh: 然而，我没有理解的是，许多人正从相似的距离和四面八方将橙子掷向马车。

sentences.en: Tracers from this circular firing squad were sailing over the carriage, were streaking past the bodies on board and whizzing straight at the people on the other side,
sentences.zh: 来自这个环形行刑队的曳光弹掠过马车，掠过车上的躯体，径直呼啸着飞向另一边的人，

sentences.en: catching shoulders, forearms, temples, mouths.
sentences.zh: 击中肩膀、前臂、太阳穴、嘴巴。

sentences.en: Seconds into the first skirmish, I took one off the crown of my head.
sentences.zh: 在第一场冲突开始几秒钟后，我的头顶挨了一下。

sentences.en: A few minutes later, a woman crossed in front of me, hollering to a companion that she'd been struck in the eye.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，一个女人从我面前走过，向同伴大喊她的眼睛被击中了。

sentences.en: I looked down to record that little moment in my notebook.
sentences.zh: 我低头把这个小插曲记在笔记本上。

sentences.en: A catastrophic mistake.
sentences.zh: 这是一个灾难性的错误。

sentences.en: I never saw the orange coming and it struck in precisely the worst possible spot.
sentences.zh: 我根本没看到橙子飞来，它精准地击中了最糟糕的部位。

sentences.en: Doubled over, staggering and groaning, panting and panicked.
sentences.zh: 弯着腰，踉踉跄跄地呻吟着，喘着粗气，惊慌失措。

sentences.en: I worried it might be serious, life-altering even.
sentences.zh: 我担心这可能会很严重，甚至会改变一生。

sentences.en: I pictured having to explain the injury to a urologist or worse, a reconstructive surgeon specializing in intimate parts.
sentences.zh: 我脑补着不得不向泌尿科医生解释这种伤情，或者更糟，向专门治疗私密部位的整形外科医生解释。

sentences.en: It took many hours for my insides to feel right.
sentences.zh: 我花了好几个小时才让体内感觉恢复正常。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星之外是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天使用不同的起始单词。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢单锅食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.zh: 《纽约

sentences.zh: 庆祝

sentences.en: 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 175年来一直帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.zh: 立即订阅，即可在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 获取特别优惠。

sentences.en: From then on, I concentrated on watching and dodging.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我专注于观看和躲闪。

sentences.en: Over the next three days,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三天里，

sentences.en: I'd see
sentences.zh: 我看到

sentences.en: Arncherry in demonic face paint and body paint and one with a bullseye scrawled on his bald head with the words throw it here.
sentences.zh: 涂着恶魔面部彩绘和身体彩绘的掷橙者，还有一个人的光头上画着靶心，上面写着“往这儿扔”。

sentences.en: I'd watch a grown woman duck for cover behind her much smaller, much older mother, both giggling as the oranges rained down.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个成年女子躲在她身材小得多、年纪大得多的母亲身后找掩护，橙子如雨般落下时，两人咯咯直笑。

sentences.en: And a slender, deadpan-faced guy walk through a piazza as the next carriage approached with a cardboard sign that said,
sentences.zh: 还有一个身材苗条、面无表情的家伙拿着一块纸板标语走过一个广场，此时下一辆马车正驶近，标语上写着：

sentences.en: My father is the first one in the carriage.
sentences.zh: “我爸在车上第一个。

sentences.en: Kill him.
sentences.zh: 杀了他。”

sentences.en: I'd watch people nonchalantly rolling cigarettes just steps from the crossfire.
sentences.zh: 我看到人们在距离交火处仅几步之遥的地方若无其事地卷烟。

sentences.en: A group of battered young people walking arm in arms saturated with juice singing When the Saints
sentences.zh: 一群浑身是伤、浑身沾满汁液的年轻人手挽着手走着，用不太完美但热情洋溢的

sentences.en: Go Marching In in imperfect but exuberant
sentences.zh: 英语

sentences.en: English.
sentences.zh: 唱着《当圣徒

sentences.zh: 列队行进》。

sentences.en: Arncherry otherwise perceived to be weak kneels on the ground while a tight circle of his teammates whips overripe oranges at his face from inches away.
sentences.zh: 我目睹了几场所谓的“洗礼”，其中一个新手或被认为虚弱的掷橙者跪在地上，而他的一群队友紧紧围成一圈，在几英寸外将过熟的橙子疯狂地朝他的脸猛砸。

sentences.en: Is that blood?
sentences.zh: “那是血吗？”

sentences.en: I'd hear one young man ask another, examining his left ear.
sentences.zh: 我听到一个年轻人问另一个人，检查着他的左耳。

sentences.zh: “是血橙。”

sentences.en: The friend clarified.
sentences.zh: 朋友澄清道。

sentences.en: Though I'd see plenty of actual blood too, crusting under nostrils, catching the sunlight on a dark, puffy lip.
sentences.zh: 尽管我也看到了很多真正的血，在鼻孔下结痂，在黑暗、红肿的嘴唇上捕捉着阳光。

sentences.en: And from time to time, whenever the throwers aboard the carriages momentarily ran out of oranges,
